findings.reason: the plan must name `judgment.py::decide_batch` as the owner it rides and add `sn-judgment-evaluation#s2` to §3's declared dependencies, or it re-creates the duplicate owner §2 exists to prevent, and the `sn-judge` seat (§3 needs it for Zeus/standard-names spend attribution) may not exist when §3 lands.
findings.text: the plan builds §3/§4 as "question and state builders" but never names the shared decisions owner `decide_batch` (also `judge_rows`:136, `rerank_pool`:179) that they must route through, and it declares no dependency on `sn-judgment-evaluation` §2 — the section that creates that owner and the `sn-judge` seat — even though its own §3 lists a rerank that `sn-selection-over-generation` §4 says is `rerank_pool` in this same file; `sn-judgment-evaluation` §2 states the rule verbatim ("delete the wrapper and route its callers through the shared owner, before a third owner appears for standard names"), and a standard-names review builder built without it is exactly that third owner, in a file the plan never opens. Second instance of the same type: the plan's §5 names the pyproject option `refine-trigger-keywords` (pyproject.toml:828) as retired but not the field that owns it, `fanout/config.py:95` — the module the change actually edits.

findings.reason: naming one module (or stating why name and docs states cannot share a builder) is what turns three thin surfaces over `decide_batch` into one deep one, and it is cheaper to decide at plan time than to reconcile two builder families after they diverge.
findings.text: §3 (name review) and §4 (docs review) each add a separate set of "question and state builders" over the same decisions machinery, and §6 adds a third layer (the cascade) over both, so the review surface is spread across three small pieces that all wrap one call owner rather than one module that hides it; nothing in §3 or §4 states whether a single builder parameterised by a question table serves both axes or why two independent sets must exist.

findings.reason: the plan should consume the existing `AuditReport` findings as checks (the pipeline already threads them into the batch), and reserve Jev questions for the failures that genuinely need judgment; as written it forks the house-style owner the sibling plan just consolidated.
findings.text: §2 admits "the house-style checks of `sn-house-style` §4" into the taxonomy, and §4 states "the house-style conformance checks are added as named checks", each of which §2 defines as carrying "one Jev question"; but `sn-house-style` §4 owns those checks as deterministic findings in this file (`run_lexical_lint`:296, `run_all_audits`:674), rules explicitly that "a second lint module is not built", and routes them to the reviewer through the `AuditReport` that the review pipeline already reads and passes as `audit_findings` (`review/pipeline.py:548`, `:1076`); re-asking a deterministic check as a Jev Noul pays a model to re-derive what code already answers.

findings.reason: the plan does account for the net surface plan-wide through §5 and §7, so this is a placement-of-the-accounting defect rather than an unaccounted addition, and moving one sentence would not change what is built.
findings.text: with all four supplied counts at 0, §2 stages a new check-taxonomy asset and a test, and §3/§4 add two builder families to public_definitions, yet none of these three sections names in its own text what it retires or merges or why nothing can be; the plan's retirements are real but live in other sections (§5 retires the keyword list, §7 retires the quorum cycles and the extra review seats), so a reader of the adding sections cannot see the net surface.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §3 and §4 add two independent question-and-state builder sets over the same decisions machinery, with no statement of whether one module builds both axes or why two must exist.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan turns the house-style conformance checks into Jev-asked named checks instead of consuming the deterministic owner in `imas_codex/standard_names/review/audits.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 stages a new check-taxonomy asset and §3/§4 add builder sets to public_definitions, and neither names what it retires or merges in its own text (the retirements sit later, in §5 and §7).
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites the review prompts and its sibling plans but never names the shared decisions owner (`imas_codex/discovery/base/judgment.py::decide_batch`) the review would run through, nor declares the dependency on the section (`sn-judgment-evaluation` §2) that creates that owner and the `sn-judge` seat.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §5 extends the existing refine prompt rendering and its fan-out trigger (`imas_codex/standard_names/fanout/trigger.py:105`), naming what it retires (the keyword list) rather than adding a parallel path; §6's shadow cascade is justified by its measurement (the incumbent quorum stays callable until §7).
